page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Hardware capabilities include 48 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptography acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), and AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 1933 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, but contains no GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput and database execution efficiency. The instance achieved upper-quartile scores in PassMark CPU (50651.26), PassMark memory (2844.62), PassMark database operations (22997.62), and PassMark CPU encryption tests (43840.97). Uncached memory bandwidth testing showed top-tier performance with 260.21 GB/sec on large-block reads and 127.25 GB/sec on writes. Static web serving throughput also ranked in the top 25% at 48.57 GB/sec. General multi-core processing performed in the middle 50%, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 15471.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 46635.68.

Without hardware GPU acceleration, performance drops noticeably in heavy execution workloads such as large-model LLM generation. For example, text generation on a 70B parameter model scored in the bottom 10% at 2.33 tokens per second, despite acceptable prompt processing across smaller models. The server's high memory density and bundled high-speed local NVMe-equivalent SSD storage make it cost-efficient for heavy memory-bound tasks where dedicated hardware accelerators are unnecessary.

The Azure E48ds_v5 is well matched for in-memory databases, large enterprise relational database instances, distributed cache deployments such as Redis clusters, high-volume static web serving, and memory-intensive ETL data processing pipelines.
